items.problem: Device-unavailable fallback message rendered twice (once as a fixed headline, once as the dynamic detail line showing the identical string).
items.evidence: discrepancies.json s1-duplicate-fallback-message; generated Scenario1_DisplayDepthColorIR.xaml line 49 (static headline TextBlock) + .xaml.cs line 102 ShowFallback("This sample requires a camera device...") setting FallbackMessage (line 50/227) to the same string.
items.covered_at: SKILL.md > Critical Rules > 'Defensive UI for device-dependent features' (Rule: 'The fallback can be as simple as a centred TextBlock saying "This sample requires a <device-kind> device that is not available on this machine." plus the exception's Message underneath.')
items.why_missed: under-emphasized / ambiguous — the wording describes a fixed headline PLUS an exception-message line, but never says the detail line is exception-ONLY. On the most common no-hardware path the device list simply comes back empty (no exception thrown), so the agent repeated the fixed headline into the detail line, duplicating it.
items.proposed_improvement: Sharpen the existing rule to state that the fallback must render the headline exactly once, and the optional second/detail line is populated ONLY from the caught exception's Message — left empty when there is no exception (e.g. the empty-device-list / 'nothing found' case). Do not hardcode the headline in XAML and also re-emit it dynamically.
items.generalizes: The Defensive-UI pattern is applied to EVERY device-dependent page in EVERY scenario (camera, microphone, location, sensors, Bluetooth, NFC). The no-device path is the DEFAULT path in the no-hardware validation environment, so a duplicate-message bug caused by this wording recurs on essentially every device-dependent migration, not just CameraFrames.
